description:
Implement the reviewed profile-format-2 envelope and cut permanent tuning ownership over from `gf2-core` to `gf2-algebra`.

## Background

The prerequisite crate-ownership design governs this task. Work test-first and preserve one process-wide installation authority. The cutover is incompatible by design: the active flat profile representation and core-owned permanent family are superseded, not retained beside the canonical form. Historical measurement evidence may remain only where the design places it as an immutable archive/receipt input; production profile discovery and loaders must not consume it.

Every serialized profile uses the same strict format-2 envelope. Owner crates publish authoritative owner-only envelopes; the repository composer links both crates and mechanically assembles the complete envelope. A loader validates every present section through a registered owner codec and rejects unknown or unregistered present sections. An absent section may resolve to its crate-owned conservative default. No partial-composite or skipped-section state is implemented.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Tests establish explicit registry construction, duplicate section-ID/type rejection, strict rejection of unknown or unregistered present sections, unsupported envelope and section version rejection, deterministic bytes independent of registration order, missing-section conservative resolution, owner-envelope to complete-envelope canonical identity, and global one-shot install/default ordering through the design's subprocess helper. The API contains no subset load mode, skipped record, skipped access branch, or compatibility reader.
- [hard] REQ-02: `gf2-core` implements the generic format-2 envelope, provenance and resolution records, typed erased codec registry using only safe Rust, deterministic encoding, first-resolution diagnostics, and the single atomic install/resolve cell. Core selector vocabulary is represented by one core-owned section and remains behaviorally identical under conservative resolution.
- [hard] REQ-03: `gf2-algebra` owns its tuning section, `PermanentSelectors`, validation, codec, active accessor, and the canonical `CHUNK_SUBSETS` default at the permanent selector source. The permanent dispatch boundary reads that section through the shared mechanism, and shared behavioral tests prove conservative equivalence, installed-value routing, and deterministic results across chunk lengths.
- [hard] REQ-04: The active committed profile/storage and every loader, baked witness, test, calibration producer, and permanent artifact are cut over exactly as the design specifies. Owner-only envelopes are authoritative, the both-codec composer emits and strictly reopens the complete envelope, and each complete section is canonically identical to its owner artifact. Serde/codecs remain non-default features, assembly and section provenance round-trip, and no build side effect or reverse production dependency is introduced.
- [hard] REQ-05: `cargo-ci`, independent code review, and documentation review pass on a final tree with no `gf2_core::tuning::PermanentSelectors`, `PERMANENT_GRAY_CHUNK_SUBSETS_DEFAULT`, core `permanent` profile family/field variants, active flat-format profile or reader, compatibility alias, partial-composite loader, skipped-section state, duplicate install authority, or present-tense prose retaining D4/DEC-B11 as the current convention.

## Notes

- Do not run a host calibration in this issue. It produces the clean canonical format-2 producer that `389aa4de` measures next.
- Preserve old receipts as taken; append supersession and archive records rather than changing measured figures.
title: Cut tuning over to crate-owned typed sections
